pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and default normal; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list text with '— high'/'— low' and none for normal.
'AC-3' test checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
'AC-4' test checks all items in id order; code unchanged for the unfiltered path.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav for all four views, current one in <strong>.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__; the code uses a Set.
'AC-7' test checks the per-priority no-match messages and 'No items yet.' in every view on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it, and the check script accepts queries.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) deleted the 'All priorities: every item, All current' state test. The 'All priorities' row of the spec's States table now has no test that sets up the state and checks it. AC-4 and AC-5 cover the list and the nav only in separate tests, so no one test covers the row.
findings.fix: Restore the deleted test, or add an equivalent test that sets up the all-priorities state and checks both the full list and All.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and that tests cover 'each state'. A test was deleted in the final commit, and the All priorities state is untested.
findings.fix: Restore the test and correct the PR text, or state the deletion and why.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line at the start of the 'states' describe block.
findings.fix: Remove the blank line when the test is restored.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and adds nothing beyond it.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and tested. The 'All priorities' state row lost its test in the last commit.
npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed; CI is declared to run the tests. The tests I read assert behaviour. A test was deleted in the last commit.
The README documents the filter. No stale text found.
Filter validation is correct. The SQL is parameterized. The traffic-config-check regex change is covered by tests.
The priority value is checked against an allow-list, SQL is bound, titles are escaped, and no planted instructions were found.
The diff touches no UI style files, only the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and the change has no screenshots or browser session.
No browser was available and the UI change is a minimal server-rendered nav.
The claims 'Tests deleted: none' and 'covers each state' are false against the final commit.
